head: A research grant can bring a group into the network.
deck: Who gave looks beyond the employees in Arrival. The wider roster includes Anthropic, its funders and leaders, and groups those funders support.
note: A tax return can list a role held for only part of the year. Federal obligations are amounts agencies committed.
bridge: Which people in that wider circle gave the most to today’s members’ committees?
source: Grant lists · House witness list · IRS returns · USAspending

head: Eric Schmidt and Reed Hastings gave 72% of the named donors’ total.
deck: This ranking uses named funders and their households, people from grantmaking groups, and people tied to Anthropic or its political groups. Arrival groups employees by their reported employer.
note: The donor pools can overlap. Gifts count at first receipt and may predate the giver’s network role.
bridge: Which types of committees took in the wider network’s gifts?

head: Joint fundraisers took in $13.7M, over twice the $6.4M given directly to candidates’ committees.
deck: These are personal gifts from named network donors and employees of network organisations. A joint fundraiser takes one gift and can split it among multiple committees.
note: Each gift counts where it first landed. Later allocations are excluded.
bridge: How much did those individuals give in earlier election cycles?
source: FEC contribution records · Where network individuals’ contributions land

head: Network individuals gave $14.2M in the partial 2026 cycle, the highest in this record.
deck: The previous high in this collection was $8.3M in the 2024 cycle.
note: These are people’s own contributions to all recipients in the collection. Recent cycles were searched more deeply, and filings for the 2026 cycle are still arriving.
bridge: Some PACs also gave money themselves. How did they compare?

head: Across all recipients here, an advocacy group’s PAC gave $434K, more than Anthropic’s PAC.
deck: Americans for Responsible Innovation is an advocacy group in the wider network. The bars show giving by each PAC itself.
note: Americans for Responsible Innovation’s PAC and ANTHROPAC draw on members’ or employees’ money. The Arnold & Porter PAC draws on partners’ money and appears here because the firm lobbied for Open Philanthropy Action Fund. The latest year is partial.
source: FEC filings and lobbying contribution reports
